milestone: Phase 3 Track A third repair pass — live browser verification of RES-2026-08-23-FSVC-DELEGATION-VS-ASSIGNMENT-ELIGIBILITY-001 confirmed the picker fix and clean admission diagnostics, but surfaced a SEPARATE, previously-unaddressed defect: every service for every consumer read FINANCIAL_SERVICES_NOT_VERIFIED.
problem: eligibility.ts unconditionally required `ctx.verification.financialServicesEligible` (Pulse + P&L verification) whenever a service declared `requiresAdmission: true` — every current catalog entry. Financial Services verification answers 'may THIS agent PERFORM Financial Services work' — a PROVIDER/specialist qualification question. Nakamoto and Kn0w1 requesting Advisor/Architect/Runtime are CONSUMERS of a MoneyPenny service, not providers of Financial Services themselves, so bundling the check into `requiresAdmission` incorrectly demanded provider-grade qualification from every consumer merely to be admitted.
observedFailure: Live browser console (dev-beta.aigentz.me, /triad/embed/codex/moneypenny-codex, Track A): both Aigent Nakamoto and Aigent Know1 showed all three services (Advisor/Architect/Runtime) as 'not eligible — FINANCIAL_SERVICES_NOT_VERIFIED', despite clean admission diagnostics (registryActivated=true, structural assignment resolvable, auditGaps=[]) confirming RES-2026-08-23-FSVC-DELEGATION-VS-ASSIGNMENT-ELIGIBILITY-001's own fix was working correctly for its intended scope.
rootCauses: eligibility.ts's `requiresAdmission` block conflated three genuinely distinct facts under one boolean: constitutional admission, structural assignment, AND Financial Services (provider-grade) verification. The first two are legitimate consumer-eligibility prerequisites; the third is a provider/specialist qualification question that has no bearing on whether an already-admitted, already-assigned agent may consume a downstream service.

No service definition had ever declared an explicit, opt-in policy for whether verification applies to its consumers — the check ran unconditionally for any service with `requiresAdmission: true`, silently treating 'admission' as if it implied 'is independently Financial-Services-qualified'.
resolution: Added `ConsumerVerificationRequirement = 'NOT_REQUIRED' | 'REQUIRED'` (types/financialServices.ts) as an explicit, opt-in field on `FinancialServiceEligibilityPolicy`, following the same house convention as `AttestationRequirement`/`ConfidentialRequirement`.

Moved the Financial Services verification check in eligibility.ts out of the `requiresAdmission` block into its own top-level check, gated behind `definition.eligibilityPolicy.consumerVerificationRequirement === 'REQUIRED'` — a service that does not opt in is eligible regardless of the consumer's verification state.

Set `consumerVerificationRequirement: 'NOT_REQUIRED'` on all three current catalog entries (MONEYPENNY_ADVISOR, MONEYPENNY_ARCHITECT, MONEYPENNY_RUNTIME) — none of them require a consumer to independently be a verified Financial Services provider.

Preserved the verification-gating MECHANISM (not deleted): a locally-constructed service with `consumerVerificationRequirement: 'REQUIRED'` still correctly resolves FINANCIAL_SERVICES_VERIFICATION_UNRESOLVED / FINANCIAL_SERVICES_NOT_VERIFIED / eligible in the same three-valued style as before, for the day a future service genuinely needs consumer-side FS qualification.
rejectedApproaches: Deleting the Financial Services verification check from eligibility.ts entirely — rejected: the check itself is not wrong, only its unconditional application to every admission-requiring service is; a future service MAY legitimately require a consumer to be independently FS-qualified, so the mechanism must remain available as an explicit opt-in rather than be removed.

Defaulting `consumerVerificationRequirement` to `REQUIRED` and only flipping the three current catalog entries to `NOT_REQUIRED` — rejected in favor of a `NOT_REQUIRED` default: the operator's ruling was explicit that admission must never be overloaded with a provider-qualification assumption; a `REQUIRED`-by-default type would re-introduce exactly that overload for any future service that forgets to declare the field.
